evidence: deepseek checks `p1_list[i] + p2_list[i] > T` and `sum(p1_list) > T`; gpt-oss checks `p1 + p2 > T` and `sum(p1_list) > T`; qwen says `The best case is Q_i uses the smallest p1 numbers`; glm accumulates `total_p1` and `total_p2` and compares them with T
affordance_in_statement: A query function Q_i mapping ... into the set {1, 2, ..., T}; a reply function R_i mapping ... into the set {1, 2, ..., T}; `Q_i` and `R_i` are injective; the images of Q_x and Q_y must be disjoint
removal_suggestion: The capacity shortcut follows intrinsically from injectivity and disjointness, so it cannot be removed by rewording alone. To defeat it, add or substitute a genuinely value-dependent compatibility condition on the mapped values (while preserving the same certificate labels and examples), so feasibility is no longer determined solely by p1+p2 and the two global sums.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses the necessary cardinality inequalities p1+p2<=T, sum(p1)<=T, and then sum(p2)<=T to classify the unique failure.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: Injective functions map into a state space of size T, and images for distinct exchanges must be disjoint.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Checks each exchange's local capacity, then applies global query and reply capacity sums.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The functions are injective into {1, 2, ..., T}, with pairwise-disjoint query and reply images.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Treats the extremal assignment as placing Q values first and R values last, reducing causality to p1+p2>T.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: Causality is expressed only through max(Q_i)<min(R_i) over the common ordered state space.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Accumulates total_p1 and total_p2 and compares each with T after checking local p1+p2 capacity.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: Pairwise disjoint injective images require the sums of their domain sizes to fit in the T-state space.

common_affordance: The statement makes every feasibility question cardinality-only: injectivity and pairwise disjointness turn the function requirements into local p1+p2 and global sum-of-p1/sum-of-p2 pigeonhole tests.
recommended_edit: Introduce a mutable, value-dependent constraint on the images—such as a prescribed residue, adjacency, or exchange-index compatibility rule—so that satisfying local and global cardinality bounds is no longer sufficient to determine the broken requirement.
regression_risk: A value-dependent rule could make previously defeated models fail for the wrong reason or accidentally restore models that currently rely on the same cardinality tests.
